rubric.why: Dynamics is a branch of mechanics concerned with motion.
rubric.description: Identifies the branch and subject of dynamics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying dynamics as a branch of mechanics that studies motion.

rubric.why: Dynamics also considers the forces that cause motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that dynamics studies the forces causing or affecting motion.

modelAnswer: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics that studies the motion of bodies and the forces that cause this motion.

items.followUp: Define the pivot and moment arm for a force acting on a lever.

rubric.why: The line of action is the imaginary line along which a force acts.
rubric.description: Defines the line of action of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the imaginary straight line along which the force acts.

rubric.why: The moment arm is measured perpendicularly from the pivot or axis to the force's line of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis of rotation to the line of action of the force.

modelAnswer: The line of action of a force is the imaginary straight line along which the force acts.
The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis of rotation to the line of action of the force.

items.followUp: Define one joule of work and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: The watt is the SI unit of power.
rubric.description: Names the SI unit of power.

rubric.why: One watt is defined as one joule of work done in one second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.

items.followUp: State Newton's First Law of Motion and explain what is meant by inertia.

rubric.why: Newton's Second Law relates the rate of change of momentum to the applied force and its direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force and occurs in the force's direction.

rubric.why: The derivation begins by expressing force as proportional to the change in momentum per unit time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing force proportional to change in momentum divided by time.

rubric.why: Using momentum and acceleration expresses the rate of change of momentum in terms of mass and acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using change in momentum = mv − mu = m(v − u) and a = (v − u)/t.

rubric.why: In SI units, the resulting equation is F = ma.
rubric.description: Obtains the equation of Newton's Second Law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deriving or stating F = ma.

modelAnswer: Newton's Second Law: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
Force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum: F ∝ (final momentum − initial momentum)/time.
For a body of constant mass m changing velocity from u to v in time t, change in momentum = mv − mu = m(v − u).
Acceleration a = (v − u)/t, so F ∝ m(v − u)/t = ma.
In SI units the proportionality constant is 1; therefore, F = ma.
